restrictions: BUILT FOR API 9, RUN ON API 16: the APK (minSdkVersion 9, libraries compiled and linked against the android-9 sysroot) was run only on an Android 4.1.2 (API 16) x86 emulator, the oldest system the project owner's emulator can run. This verdict says nothing about Android 2.3 (API 9) to 4.0 (API 15): they were NOT run, so the floor of the Android Legacy UI is NOT validated, and the words 'works on Android 2.3' are not supported by any evidence. What the build does establish: the x86 library links with --no-undefined against the API 9 libc and needs only libc.so and libdl.so.

ONE EMULATED SYSTEM: Android emulator 37.2.13.0 with the AOSP image android-16 default x86 (4.1.2, build eng.wdu.20191218.182616, 2 vCPUs, 1,024 MB, WHPX) started headless with swiftshader_indirect: not a phone, no real GPU, touch screen, vendor skin, vendor fonts or input method. display_ms (123 to 161 ms in the stored lines) and peak_rss_kb (38,724) are the emulator's and indicative only. No other API level (17 to 23, 24+) and no x86_64 or ARM system was started.

ONLY THE x86 LIBRARY WAS EXECUTED: the same APK holds armeabi, armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a libraries, built and checked (needed libraries, exported symbols) but never run; their platforms have not_tested verdicts (android-2.3-arm, android-5.0-arm64). The x86 run does not prove them.

INPUT WAS SYNTHETIC: the window run typed 'Marie' with `adb shell input keyevent` / `input text` (typing-uiautomator.txt) and read the screen with uiautomator, never a person, a hardware keyboard or an input method of a vendor. The update delay of the greeting (User Story 1, within 1 second) was not measured (a 2 s wait before the dump). The 1,000-character limit was exercised through the probe input only (the two vectors of 4,096 characters were cut to 1,000 UTF-16 units by the field's input filter), not by typing 1,001 characters. No screenshot was taken or stored.

TEXT GIVEN BY TWO ROUTES: the plain intent extra `probe_input` for the texts the `am` command can carry, and `probe_input_file` (a UTF-8 file pushed with adb) for a text with a character outside the BMP or longer than 1,500 bytes, because `am` of Android 4.1 crashes with a segmentation fault in Check_NewStringUTF on a 4-byte UTF-8 sequence (measured) and adb refuses a 4,096-byte command ('shell command too long'). Both routes reach the same EditText.setText; the emoji vectors passed through the file route only.

GLYPHS: the probe checks the text of the greeting character for character (15 of 15 vectors, including CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, emoji and a ZWJ sequence); how the 4.1.2 emulator draws them (fonts, missing glyph boxes, bidi) was not looked at, since no screenshot was taken.

NOT CHECKED: dark and high-contrast themes (the UI uses the system theme colours, the end-of-life banner has fixed black on #FFF3CD), 4.5:1 contrast of the greeting, rotation, screen sizes other than 1080x1920, accessibility services, a build signed with anything but a debug key, installation from a store, the behaviour when the process is killed. The exit of the UI is `finish()` 2 s after the first display; Android keeps the process cached, so 'exit status 0' is not measured, the launcher checks that the activity is no longer resumed and that logcat has no FATAL EXCEPTION.

ONE DAY, ONE MACHINE: runs of 2026-11-14 (the vectors three times in the session, the last one stored). The first vector run of the session failed 4 vectors because of the launcher (emoji through `am`, long input through the shell command) and one vector took 17.9 s once (cjk, cause not investigated); after the file route was added the 15 vectors passed in 49 s in every later run. The backend self-test (loomora_selftest, all vectors) also passed on the emulator.

notes: Verdict of the Android Legacy UI (Java views, JNI glue, C++11 backend) on the x86 emulator at API 16, written 2026-11-14 after real runs. STATUS ok_restricted: the greeting 'Bonjour Coucou' / 'Bonjour Marie' is computed by the backend and displayed, typing updates it, the end-of-life banner shows, the 15 reference vectors pass and the self-test passes, but the restrictions above are real: built for API 9 and run on API 16 only, one emulator, x86 only, synthetic input, no screenshot. DECISION keep: nothing found makes the UI unusable on this system, and the API 9 floor stays an open question that only a system or emulator of API 9 to 15 can answer (the emulator of this project cannot start below API 16). RERUN OF 2026-11-15, AFTER THE PACKAGE RENAME TO fr.bansan.loomora: the evidence above (probe line, vectors, self-test, typing, screenshots, build output, apk sha256 d4b0d066...) was produced by the APK built on 2026-11-14 with the earlier package id fr.loomora.probe, and it is history, not edited. The deliverable record of this platform now describes the rebuilt APK (python tools/build.py android legacy: 228,663 bytes, sha256 7eb8d186b4bf3447000b756fd6a3357aa146a7b359bbb1f4de48211dccfd5b6b, package fr.bansan.loomora.probe, same four libraries of the same sizes), so this verdict refers to a DIFFERENT build than its stored evidence. What was rerun on the rebuilt APK, not stored again (ADR 0014): python tools/run_vectors.py android-4.1.2-x86 legacy on the same kind of API 16 x86 emulator (AVD API16, headless): 15 vectors, 15 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped, 2 truncated to 1,000 UTF-16 units, 43.8 s. NOT rerun on the rebuilt APK: the loomora_selftest of the x86 ABI (the binary changed by 8 bytes, sha256 fadda1fd..., not pushed to the emulator), the typing check and the screenshots. The restrictions above still hold unchanged. SPEC 002 (.loomora project file), runs of 2026-11-17 on this platform's emulator (Android emulator 37.2.13.0, AVD API16 = android-16 default x86, headless, WHPX; one Windows 11 host, which the other spec 002 records identify as an Intel Core i7-11800H, not the MSI laptop of validation/platforms/windows-11-x64.json; android_results.json names no CPU), recorded 2026-11-18. This paragraph REPLACES the first version of 2026-11-17, which said not_tested because the NDK r15c and an emulator were not installed; they were installed afterwards (validation/results/spec-002/android_results.md, branch feat/fmt-android) and the runs below were made. TOOLCHAIN: NDK r15c (15.2.4203891, Clang 5.0.300080) downloaded as a zip from dl.google.com (849,733,996 bytes, SHA-256 6f3785cb...bcd8d); no published checksum was found to compare it with (the hash is the measured one), the archive extracted without error. BUILT FOR API 9, RUN ON API 16: the x86 test programs were built against the android-9 sysroot (not PIE) and run on API 16 only; nothing from API 9 to 15 was run, so the Android 2.3 floor is still not validated by this run. FORMAT RESULT: loomora_selftest passed (all vectors), loomora_format_selftest passed, the S-F1 spike printed 'S-F1: ok' with the three lines of the other targets, and loomora_refgen wrote the six reference files (basic, empty, escape40, multi, multi-light, one) whose SHA-256 are identical to the reference, with no switch (Clang for x86 uses SSE2; spike S-F2; the hashes are in validation/evidence/adr-0021/android-4.1.2-x86/hashes.json, the files are byte-identical to those stored under windows-11-x64/ and are not stored again, ADR 0014). THE FALLBACK android-api9-lseek64 IS THE CODE THAT RAN: LOOMORA_FMT_LSEEK64 is on below API 21, so core/src/format/io/file_posix.cpp used the pread64 / pwrite64 system calls through syscall() (API < 12) and fstat() (API < 21). The first compile with r15c FAILED (pread64, pwrite64 and fstat64 are undeclared in the unified headers before API 12 / 21 and absent from the libc of API 9 to 11); the code was fixed (see fallbacks.json) and the gnustl of the NDK, which has no std::to_string, got a local helper. NOT RUN on Android: a file above 2 GiB (the 5 GiB tests are host only), so the offset split of the system call was never exercised above 2 GiB. SC-010 (T091, tools/run_vectors.py --validate-project and --roundtrip-project against `loomora validate --quiet` of the g++ build in WSL): the Legacy UI (Java views, JNI bridge) matched in 37 of 37 runs (the 6 loomora_refgen files written on the emulator and the 9 valid-* corpus files validated and round-tripped, one invalid file, one missing path, 3 usage rows); the whole generated corpus (113 files, validate only, with the hostile and large ones) and the 3 usage rows matched in 116 of 116; the 15 reference vectors passed again (15 passed, 16 skipped, 49.8 s). The activity of a project mode finishes at once and has no exit status: the launcher infers the status from the line (android_project_status) and does not use `am start -W`. THIS RUN WAS MADE WITH THE APK OF 2026-11-17 (loomora.apk, 4 ABIs, 1,472,418 bytes, sha256 2b008181afd19b25ebf2b742b24ba09712159a0cb0cbce1d5255d32327aade8a, built by tools/build.py android legacy with the format code), NOT with the APK of the deliverable record (228,663 bytes, sha256 7eb8d186...): that record was not rewritten (tools/build.py writes it only when the docs submodule is checked out, which it was not), so this verdict refers to another build than its deliverable record, as already noted above. NOT RUN and not claimed: the armeabi, armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a libraries and test programs (built and checked as ELF files, never run: no ARM system, so the ARM EABI padding argument of the pread64 system call is never executed), Android 2.3 to 4.0, any other API level than 16 (API 24 and 35 are in android-7.0-x86_64-modern.json), files above 2 GiB, a real phone. The status of this verdict is unchanged.
